title: Indonesian mass killings of 1965-66
summary: After senior Indonesian generals were kidnapped and killed on 30 September 1965, an anti-leftist purge of suspected communists swept Indonesia in 1965-66. Death-toll estimates differ: about 500,000 in scholarly accounts, 600,000 to 1 million from the National Commission on Human Rights, and 2 million from one former general. Robinson argues the Army led a deliberate campaign, with more than a million detained.

uncertainty.note: Sources give the span as 1965-66, with the generals killed on 30 September 1965.

audience_note: Describes mass killing and mass detention of suspected communists. Death tolls are contested estimates that vary widely by source and method.

beats.caption: Senior Indonesian generals were kidnapped and killed on 30 September 1965; a purge of suspected communists followed.
Indonesia’s National Commission on Human Rights estimated the purge killed between 600,000 and 1 million people; other estimates differ.
Robinson concludes the violence was a deliberate Army-led campaign that left some 500,000 dead and over a million detained.

reviewer_note: Toll is attributed, not asserted: ~500,000 (Princeton UP blurb, Chandra), 600,000-1 million (National Commission on Human Rights via NPR, 2012), about 2 million (a former general, per NPR). Pin is Java as a coarse locator; killings were archipelago-wide. Least sure: exact start date of the purge.
